GitHub - nodejs/Release: Node.js Release Working Group

github.com/nodejs/Release
There are three phases that a Node.js release can be in: 'Current', 'Active Long Term Support (LTS)', and 'Maintenance'. Odd-numbered release lines are not promoted to LTS - they will not go through the 'Active LTS' or 'Maintenance' phases. Current - Should incorporate most of the non-major (non-breaking) changes that land on nodejs/node main branch. Active LTS - New features, bug fixes, and ...

Node.js - endoflife.date

endoflife.date/nodejs
Major Node.js versions enter Current release status for six months, which gives library authors time to add support for them. After six months, releases after 26 move to Active LTS status and are ready for general use. Node.js 24 Becomes LTS: What You Need to Know

nodesource.com/blog/nodejs-24-becomes-lts
With the release of Node.js 24.11. "Krypton", the Node.js 24 line has officially entered Long-Term Support (LTS) and will continue receiving maintenance and security updates through April 2028. This marks the beginning of a new stable era for production workloads, bringing developers enhanced security, stricter runtime behavior, and improved Web API support.
